Score: attack path is a JSON-RPC call, attacker-controlled fields but it's a direct tool call, not natural language to a privileged decision. LC: attacker supplies structured JSON, not NL influencing agent behavior... The register_tool args include name/description strings — direct attacker-supplied data reaching tool registry. It's not language influencing a model; but description could be NL. I'd say LC = D (direct)? The path is a direct tool-invocation with attacker-supplied input reaching registry — "attacker-supplied natural language reaches a privileged decision or tool-invocation path without mediation" — the description string reaches tool registry directly. LC=D.

CP: registration persists in agent.tools (in-memory, server lifetime, cross-request) — session context? It's in the agent process memory, persists beyond a session across requests. Rubric: session context = ephemeral session state; cross-session memory = durable stores. In-memory agent.tools is not a durable store but persists across requests/sessions. Hmm. It's not durable (restart clears) but persists beyond a single session. CP rubric: C requires durable stores; S is ephemeral session state confirmed unreachable after session boundary. Registry persists across sessions but not durable. I'll pick C? "vector databases, long-term agent memory..." — tools array in memory isn't durable. Between S and C: not testing-confirmed ephemeral. I'll say C, medium... Actually in-memory across sessions — safer to call S? Rubric S says "persists only in ephemeral session state ... testing confirms unreachable after session boundary" — that's not the case here. C says "durable stores ... remains reachable after the originating session ends" — remains reachable after session ends, yes, but in-memory not durable. I'll choose C with medium confidence, since it persists after the session.

AP: contained — effect on PluginBot's own registry within same agent; other agents could... registered tools only affect pluginbot. AP=C or N? Effect confined to PluginBot's tool list; other components unaffected. AP=N? "confined to initially affected component" — yes, N. But tools/list advertised to other callers... still same agent. AP=N, or C if influence relays across components under same principal. Registration is in PluginBot only; agents.js says other agents keep stateless reply. AP=N.

RH: is there a proxy/evaluator on the path? Success criteria pattern in challenges tracks attack success; the scoring logic is in the same process (attackSuccessful flags). The successCriteria pattern is the evaluator — agent (PluginBot) can... the server sets attackSuccessful=true itself; is there a reward channel reachable? The agent process contains the evaluator. Reachable proxy = true? The response text is scored against pattern; agent output feeds the grader. No verified episodes. RH=P, locus evaluator, reachable_proxy=true, verified_episodes=0.

ES: dynamic tool registration with no verification — ES=W.

CVSS: AV — default binds loopback; Docker publishes on 127.0.0.1. Attacker needs network access to loopback → local? Entry point is network JSON-RPC but only reachable on loopback by default. AV=L (attacker needs local access or a local user). Hmm, documented default deployment: Docker image binds 0.0.0.0 inside container but ports published on 127.0.0.1. Attacker on same machine → AV=A? Adjacent network requires shared logical adjacent network. Loopback-only means attacker needs local access: AV=L. PR=N (no auth), UI=N, AC=L, AT=N.

Impact: registering a tool entry — does it get executed? "A registered tool gets no new handler." So typosquatted tool entry is advertised but executing it... executeMcpTool finds it in agent.tools; the tool entry exists, call succeeds with canned reply? Impact is low: integrity of tool registry — VI=L (registry modification), VC=N/low, VA=N. Subsequent: none significant. VC:N, VI:L, VA:N, SC:N, SI:N, SA:N.

Vector: CVSS:4.0/AV:L/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:L/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N

Applicability: as implemented, no model directed goal pursuit (simulated mode, no LLM, tools scripted) — model_directed_goal_pursuit false, selects_or_sequences_actions false. As modeled: also false — no tools passed to model even in LLM mode. Both false.

Automatable: Yes — scripted curl, no human action beyond attacker.

Technical impact: Partial.
